New National Telecom Policy
*241. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has recently
formulated a new National Telecom Policy-
2011;
(b) if so, the salient features thereof
and the manner in which the policy
proposes to bring transparency in the
telecom sector and give benefits to the
consumers;
(c) whether suggestions from various
stakeholders, including telecom industry,
were acted upon by Government;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) whether roaming charges have been
dispensed with, under the new policy; and
(f) if so, the details thereof and the time
by when the new policy is likely to be
introduced and implemented?
MSP for paddy, wheat and coarse grains
*242. SHRI SHYAMAL
CHAKRABORTY: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
is buying crops at far below the market
price;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) the Minimum Support Price (MSP)
fixed for paddy, wheat and coarse grains
for the year 2010 and 2011, respectively;
and
(d) the market price of these products
in the corresponding year?
Introduction of more trains in
Andhra Pradesh
*243. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
Will the Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of the
rush of passengers for trains like Godavari
Express, Gowthami Express and the
Venkatadri Express in Andhra Pradesh;
(b) if so, the reasons for not introducing
more trains on these sectors;
(c) whether there is a shortage of railway
coaches, particularly in South-Central
Railway, or tracks in these sectors; and

(d) the details of steps that would be
taken to introduce more trains in such
sectors?
Flood and soil erosion in Assam
*244. SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD
BAISHYA: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) the details of cultivable land and crop
land rendered infertile during floods in
Assam this year;
(b) whether Government has proposed
any provision to compensate the farmers
who lost their cultivable land during floods
and erosion in Assam for the last three years
and the current year; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Gauge conversion on Ratlam-Mhow-
Khandwa railway line
†*245. SHRI MEGHRAJ JAIN: Will
the Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government has taken a
decision of gauge conversion on the Ratlam-
Mhow-Khandwa railway line;
(b) if so, by when the work would start
and by when it would be completed;
(c) the amount earmarked in the budget
for this purpose; and
(d) the details thereof?
Scholarship for girl child
*246. SHRI MOHD. ALI KHAN: Will
the Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether scholarship for girl child of
Group D railway employees has been
increased to ` 1200 per month;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the amount earmarked and spent so
far, zone-wise, especially in South-Central
Railway for the current financial year?
Loss due to train accidents
*247. SHRI T.M. SELVAGANA-
PATHI: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Railways are suffering a net
loss of over ` 100 crore per annum due to
train accidents;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Railways have suffered a
loss of over ` 10,000 crore during the last
two decades;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) whether most of the train accidents
in the world take place in our country?
Representation of SCs and STs in
institutions of National Importance
*248. SHRIMATI T. RATNA BAI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the percentage of staff and students
of institutions of National Importance
represented by members of Scheduled
Castes and Scheduled Tribes-communities
in the last five years;
(b) the details thereof;
(c) whether any measures, over and
above those ensured by concerned
legislation and court rulings, have been taken
to secure adequate representation of these
communities;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the number of drop-outs, in the
aforementioned institutions amongst
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

76
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Increase in consumption of fertilizers
vis-a-vis agricultural production
*249. PROF. ANIL KUMAR
SAHANI: Will the Minister of
CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether consumption of fertilizers
has increased by 46 per cent from the year
2003-04 to 2008-09 and whether
agricultural production has increased by just
16 per cent over the same period;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether the pattern of fertilizer
consumption across different States is
highly skewed;
(d) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(e) whether subsidised fertilizers are
used for non-agricultural purposes and are
also smuggled in border districts of Eastern/
North-Eastern States; and
(f) the measures taken to check the
misuse of subsidised fertilizers?
Agreement with Government of
Sri Lanka
*250. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Railways have entered into
an agreement with Government of Sri Lanka
for a $ 149 million reconstruction project;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether this project would require
further investment from Government; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Exemption of Government teachers
from non-teaching activities
†*251. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that teachers of
Government schools are still being used in
non-teaching works;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
National Knowledge Commission had
expressed concern over it;
(c) the extent to which Government
agrees with the concerns of the
Commission; and
(d) the steps taken by Government for
exempting Government teachers from non-
teaching works?
Slaughtering of cows/bullocks
*252. SHRI M. RAMA JOIS: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) the number of slaughter houses for
slaughtering cows/bullocks in the country
on the date of commencement of the
Constitution;
(b) the number of slaughter houses for
slaughtering cows/bullocks at present; and
(c) the steps proposed to be taken to
implement Article 48 of the Constitution?
IT equipments and computers for
institutions and schools
†*253. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of COMMUNI-
CATIONS AND INFORMATION
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government intends to

77
provide IT equipments to Governmental
and Non-Governmental institutions;
(b) if not, the time by when free
assistance of computers, etc. would be
provided to at least all schools of backward
areas, so that their capabilities can also be
utilized;
(c) whether Government is aware of the
fact that as on date, private institutions,
which are in abundance, cannot be helped
even from MPLADs funds; and
(d) whether this would be considered
and action plan would be formulated?
Remunerative price to farmers
*254. SHRI KANJIBHAI PA TEL: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has recently
announced Minimum Support Price (MSP)
for certain crops;
(b) if so, the details thereof, crop-wise;
and
(c) the steps taken/proposed to be taken
by Government to ensure remunerative
price to the farmers for their produce?
National Mission on Seeds
*255. DR. K.P. RAMALINGAM: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the long pending proposal
for a National Mission on Seeds is to be
implemented in the Twelfth Five Year Plan;
(b) whether Planning Commission has
also given its approval for the Mission to
ensure easy availability of high quality of
certified seeds to farmers at reasonable
prices; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and the steps
taken by Government in this regard?
Food Processing Industries in
Kashmir valley
*256. PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ: Will
the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that public sector
is non-existent in Kashmir valley; and
(b) if so, whether Government would
agree to establish some food processing
industries there, which are comparatively
less capital intensive and are pollution-free?
MSP of wheat
*257. SHRI PRABHAT JHA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government has increased
Minimum Support Price (MSP) of Rabi
crops including wheat during October,
2011;
(b) if so, the details thereof, crop-wise;
(c) whether Commission for
Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) has
recommended for increase of ` 230/- per
quintal in MSP of wheat;
(d) if so, the reasons for increasing the
MSP of wheat by only ` 165/- per quintal;
(e) whether Government would review
the MSP of wheat; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?
Level of food processing in the
country
*258. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:

78
(a) whether India ranks first in
production of milk, pulses and tea and
second in production of fruits and
vegetables in the world, but the country's
share in the world food trade is less than
two per cent;
(b) whether the level of food processing
in the country is abysmally low at six per
cent compared to the developed countries
and even other Asian and Latin American
countries;
(c) whether very high wastage and very
low value addition in the country causes
loss to farm income;
(d) if so, the statistics and the status of
food processing in the country, State-wise
and their comparison with other countries;
and
(e) the remedial steps taken thereon?
Steps to make BSNL profitable
*259. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
losses of Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited
(BSNL) have increased manifold in the past
few years;
(b) if so, the facts and the details thereof;
(c) whether Government proposes to
take any effective steps to make BSNL
profitable; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Development of railway lines in
Gujarat
*260. SHRIMATI SMRITI ZUBIN
IRANI: Will the Minister of RAILWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Railways have received any
request from Government of Gujarat for
development of various railway lines, for
overall development of Delhi-Mumbai
Industrial Corridor (DMIC);
(b) if so, by when Railways intend to
start these projects; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 3rd December, 2011 Secretary-General.
Agrahayana 12, 1933 (Saka)
